demos.title: One joint, two connections
demos.blurb: Move a shared joint and see why a point at the same coordinate can stay behind.
demos.context: Imagine two pieces of a linkage meeting at a pin. Sharing the pin is a structural relationship. Merely drawing their ends at the same position does not create it.
demos.focus: Root 0: ordered frames, opposed faces and shared tick references.
demos.validation: The fixture checks shared tick identity, independent equal coordinates, reversed traversal and preservation through numeric transport.
demos.limit: This establishes site identity and an explicit structural retargeting. It does not simulate the forces in a mechanical linkage.

steps.label: Shared pin
steps.title: Connected at one site
steps.text: Both directed segments refer to the same tick at 3. The nearby lookalike also reads 3, but owns a different tick.
steps.keep: Coordinate equality and site identity remain separate.

steps.label: Retarget
steps.title: The shared site moves to 5
steps.text: An explicit structural edit moves the shared tick. Both connected ends follow; the independent lookalike remains at 3.
steps.keep: Carrier value has not changed. Moving a site is a different action.

steps.label: Reverse the frame
steps.title: Direction is another read
steps.text: The original ordinary frame runs from −4 to 3. Reading its reverse runs from 3 to −4. This is a separate view of the initial fixture, not another edit.
steps.keep: Opposed flow faces, negative coordinates and reversed order each retain their own meaning.

demos.title: A position needs a frame
demos.blurb: Read 40% and 47% along a span, keeping the detail a coarser parameter leaves out.
demos.context: A slider controls a position along a rail from 10 to 210. Its local parameter runs from 0 to 100. The parameter and the rail use different scales.
demos.focus: Root 1: normalized parameter, calibration and retained refinement.
demos.validation: The kernel projects both parameter samples into the rail basis and verifies that coarsening 47 retains seven parameter ticks.
demos.limit: The frame defines parameter position. It does not make that parameter an arc-length measurement on an arbitrary curve.

steps.title: Two scales, one correspondence
steps.text: 40 on the parameter axis maps to 90 on the rail: start at 10, then traverse 40% of its 200-tick extent.
steps.keep: Both ordered frames remain attached to the observation.

steps.title: Ask for more detail
steps.text: The finer parameter sample maps to 104. This refines the view without changing the calibration.
steps.keep: The earlier 40% sample remains a valid observation of its own selected position.

steps.label: Coarse read
steps.title: Keep what the coarse view omits
steps.text: At ten parameter ticks per coarse tick, 47 reads as 4 coarse ticks with 7 parameter ticks left over.
steps.keep: The remainder is known detail, not a random error. Observation moves no material.

demos.title: Knowing x before knowing y
demos.blurb: An unfinished point can already yield a useful coordinate, without filling its unknowns with zero.
demos.context: You are locating a point one third of the way between two controls. One control’s vertical coordinate is still unknown. The horizontal calculation can nevertheless be complete.
demos.focus: Roots 0–4: partial interpolation, exact fractions and explicit support.
demos.validation: Selected interpolation returns x = 0 with an open y, then an exact 7/3 when the premise is complete. Separate requests test refused and permitted extrapolation.
demos.limit: The steps compare separately authored requests. These are chosen local reads; there is no automatic search for missing coordinates or permission to extrapolate.

steps.label: Open coordinate
steps.title: A useful partial answer
steps.text: From x = −1 to x = 2, the one-third sample is x = 0. The unknown second y keeps the output y open.
steps.keep: The known coordinate is usable. The missing one is not silently replaced by zero.

steps.label: Complete premise
steps.title: An exact fractional result
steps.text: With the second control at (2, 3), the same interpolation gives y = 7/3.
steps.keep: The fraction stays exact in the structure; drawing it uses a display approximation.

steps.label: Outside support
steps.title: A formula needs a permitted domain
steps.text: A sample at 4 lies outside the declared 0…3 support. A calculable formula alone does not authorize this read.
steps.keep: The rejected request and its participating frames remain available.

steps.label: Wider support
steps.title: Explicitly allow extrapolation
steps.text: A separately authored request permits −3…6 while keeping the same 0…3 calibration. Sample 4 can now be read.
steps.keep: Changing support changes the permission, not the underlying affine law.

demos.title: A curve from six local steps
demos.blurb: Build a Bézier sample by repeatedly taking a point between two points.
demos.context: Four controls shape a curved handle. To locate its point at t = 1/2, each little calculation only needs two inputs and the same parameter frame.
demos.focus: Root 1: six interpolation requests and their shared parameter; root 0 supplies the controls.
demos.validation: The six exact reads agree with an independent Bernstein polynomial at nine parameter samples, including endpoints. Tests also cover open, closed, repeated and reversed controls.
demos.limit: The drawn curve is a presentation of the control recipe. The selected sample and its intermediate points are checked Gojo reads. t = 1/2 is not generally halfway along arc length.

steps.label: Controls
steps.title: Four controls describe a curve
steps.text: The inner points influence the curve; the curve need not pass through them. The construction exposes all four inputs.
steps.keep: The parameter frame and the ordered control sequence are part of the request.

steps.label: First layer
steps.title: Three local interpolations
steps.text: At one half, take the midpoint of each adjacent pair. These three reads can be understood independently.
steps.keep: Each result keeps its two input participants and its read witness.

steps.label: Second layer
steps.title: Use the results as new inputs
steps.text: Interpolate between the first two results, then the last two. The next layer consumes the actual preceding results.
steps.keep: Shared results create visible dependencies between local calculations.

steps.label: Curve sample
steps.title: One last interpolation
steps.text: The midpoint of (4, 4) and (8, 3) is the curve sample at this parameter.
steps.keep: Six simple relations have produced one exact sample of a higher-level shape.

demos.title: A control moves. What stays true?
demos.blurb: Follow an edit through local dependencies, pending work and preserved history.
demos.context: We have sampled a curved handle at t = 1/2. Now its first inner control rises from (4, 8) to (4, 16). The old answer still explains the old handle.
demos.focus: Root 0: transformations, inputs and the edit. Root 1: open outline for the recorded replay and timeline.
demos.validation: The fixture discovers eight producer-consumer edges, rejects premature mixed-version replay, carries unaffected observations and resumes a restored paused graph without rewriting history.
demos.limit: The driver selects the edit and replay order. This example requires fresh premises for a current sample; a separately declared provisional or coarser use of history could still be useful.

steps.label: Original
steps.title: The original answer has its premises
steps.text: Six curve calculations produced (6, 7/2). Their input references explain which observations depend on which controls.
steps.keep: The independent lookalike calculation has equal numbers but different identity.

steps.label: Move control
steps.title: Current work becomes pending
steps.text: Five of the six curve calculations depend on the changed control. The final sample is pending under this example’s freshness contract.
steps.keep: The old sample remains historical evidence. The third first-layer calculation is unaffected.

steps.label: First calculations
steps.title: Refresh what is ready
steps.text: The first two local reads now give (2, 8) and (6, 8). The unchanged third result (10, 2) is carried forward.
steps.keep: A read cannot be called refreshed while one of its affected producers is still stale.

steps.label: New sample
steps.title: New result, preserved old result
steps.text: The remaining reads give (4, 8), (8, 5), then (6, 13/2). Both versions and their correspondence remain inspectable.
steps.keep: History still contains (6, 7/2), tied to the earlier control version.

demos.title: Touching is only the first promise
demos.blurb: Check position, tangent and second derivative separately at a curve join.
demos.context: Two drawn sections meet at one shared endpoint. A smooth-looking join can hide a stronger mismatch, especially when the path will guide motion or further construction.
demos.focus: Root 0: endpoint and first derivatives. Root 3: second-derivative construction and claim.
demos.validation: Endpoint displacement and first-derivative displacement are zero. Second-derivative displacement is (0, 6) under the shared normalized parameter. A zero derivative is not accepted as a regular tangent.
demos.limit: C1 and C2 here refer to the same declared parameter. Curvature is a separate open relationship requiring a metric and regularity evidence.

steps.label: Position
steps.title: The sections share an endpoint
steps.text: Both sections use the very same point at (3, 0). Endpoint displacement is zero, with identity evidence as well as matching coordinates.
steps.keep: A separate point at (3, 0) would give coordinate agreement without becoming the shared joint.

steps.label: First derivative
steps.title: The first derivatives agree
steps.text: Cubic endpoint derivatives are three times the adjacent control legs. Both read (3, 0) in this common parameter basis.
steps.keep: This supports C1 for the selected parameter, a stronger promise than merely meeting.

steps.label: Second derivative
steps.title: The next promise does not hold
steps.text: The second derivatives are (0, 0) and (0, 6). The join passes the previous read but fails this stronger equality claim.
steps.keep: This mismatch belongs to the statement. It does not identify which control, requirement or premise should change.

demos.title: A pattern with an open horizon
demos.blurb: Translate and reflect a motif while preserving its joints and the rule that repeats it.
demos.context: A triangular motif repeats along a decorative border. Instead of storing an endless row of copies, retain the motif, a transformation and the connection from one result to the next input.
demos.focus: Root 0: repeat/controller/window. Root 2: exposed motif maps and correspondence.
demos.validation: Actual exposed-site mapping preserves the triangle’s shared joints. Two glides and one translation have equal coordinates. An inverse returns coordinates without reviving source identity.
demos.limit: The window illustration displays five selected cells. Repeat support remains open; this does not run an autonomous infinite expander or classify every frieze group.

steps.label: Motif
steps.title: Three edges share three sites
steps.text: The triangle’s edges reuse their endpoint references. Its corners are actual joints, not separate coincident drawings.
steps.keep: Exposing the three sites tells the map precisely which participation it may transform.

steps.label: Glide
steps.title: Translate, then reflect
steps.text: The selected map adds 6 to x and negates y. It keeps a correspondence from each source site to its mapped site.
steps.keep: Reflection changes the coordinate read; it does not erase the source or its history.

steps.label: Compose
steps.title: Two glides make a translation
steps.text: The second glide reverses y again and advances another 6. It agrees with the independently selected 12-tick translation.
steps.keep: Equal final coordinates still retain their different construction routes.

steps.label: Window
steps.title: The view has edges; the rule need not
steps.text: Here are five cells of the border. The display window is finite while the controller’s overall support remains open.
steps.keep: The pattern retains its transition and feedback, rather than claiming the visible copies are the whole pattern.

demos.title: The same cup is not another cup
demos.blurb: See why shared uncertainty cancels, while a repeated description does not.
demos.context: Two quantities are each described as “about one cup.” The description alone does not say they have the same volume. Subtracting one quantity from itself is a different operation.
demos.focus: Root 0: quantity identity, description reuse and repeated participation. Root 1: shared bias and separate observation events.
demos.validation: Closed affine support reads yield [90,110], [0,0] and [−20,20] in hundredths of a cup. Shared quantity and bias cancel between two events, leaving [−2,2] event noise.
demos.limit: These are bounds conditional on the stated premises, not normal distributions or probability estimates. Distinct slots do not prove statistical independence.

steps.label: About one cup
steps.title: A quantity with a connected range
steps.text: For this example, the quantity is supported between 0.9 and 1.1 cups. Its open slot identifies which unknown quantity the range describes.
steps.keep: The phrase “about” has no universal numeric width; this fixture supplies the bounds explicitly.

steps.label: Same quantity
steps.title: A minus that exact A
steps.text: Both terms refer to the same unresolved quantity. Their coefficients cancel, whatever value within the support is eventually observed.
steps.keep: The cancellation retains its shared-source evidence.

steps.label: Different quantity
steps.title: A minus another “about one cup”
steps.text: B has the same description but a different quantity slot. Without a tighter connected relation, the difference can range from −0.2 to 0.2 cups.
steps.keep: A repeated category is not evidence that two samples are identical.

steps.label: Two observations
steps.title: Cancel shared causes; retain separate noise
steps.text: Two observations share the same quantity and calibration bias. Each also has its own event error of ±0.01 cup. Subtraction removes only the shared causes.
steps.keep: A source can remain opaque while exposing enough local correspondence for this read.

demos.title: A useful gap is not an error
demos.blurb: Keep nominal size, measured variation and desired clearance as different structures.
demos.context: A bolt must fit through a hole. We want a little room between them. Equality of their diameters would be the wrong target for this example.
demos.focus: Root 3: illustrative bolt/hole supports, two clearance specifications and nominal stops.
demos.validation: The observed clearance is [0.10,0.30] mm. Distance from the broad allowed interval is exactly zero; the narrower specification leaves possible violation [0,0.05] mm.
demos.limit: These dimensions are illustrative, not a fastener standard. Treating a tolerance as an actual-value bound requires a conformance premise.

steps.label: Actual supports
steps.title: Separate the two quantities
steps.text: The bolt is supported at 9.90…10.00 mm and the hole at 10.10…10.20 mm. Their difference is a clearance range.
steps.keep: Nominal catalogue stops such as 10, 11 and 12 mm are a separate structure.

steps.label: Allowed gap
steps.title: Every supported value is acceptable
steps.text: If the desired clearance is 0.10…0.30 mm, every possible clearance in this example meets that condition.
steps.keep: The actual size difference remains visible even though this requirement calls for no correction.

steps.label: Tighter requirement
steps.title: The answer can remain unsettled
steps.text: For a required 0.15…0.25 mm gap, some supported states fit and others lie outside. More information or a changed construction may be useful.
steps.keep: A mismatch read does not decide whether to revise the hole, bolt, measurement or requirement.

demos.title: Open a pack. Account for every unit.
demos.blurb: Split, regroup and borrow whole packets while keeping unpaid demand visible.
demos.context: A store has three packs, with ten small units in each. Opening a pack changes how stock is represented and available. Merely looking at it in smaller units would not move anything.
demos.focus: Roots 1–3: selected refinement, regrouping and borrow calibration.
demos.validation: The kernel applies the authored 1:10 transfer, preserves the seven-unit remainder on regrouping, holds a three-unit unpaid draw as negative tension, then explicitly borrows one pack.
demos.limit: Opening and borrowing are selected actions in this fixture. A general automatic inventory allocator or downward-refinement scheduler is not supplied.

steps.label: Stock
steps.title: Three packs, thirty small units
steps.text: The coarse carrier holds 3. The fine carrier holds 0. A 1:10 calibration connects their units.
steps.keep: This is stock under a declared calibration, not three and zero unrelated scalars.

steps.label: Open two
steps.title: A material action changes both stores
steps.text: Transfer two coarse ticks into twenty fine ticks. The total remains thirty small units.
steps.keep: The transfer drains the coarse source and adds to the fine receiver through settlement.

steps.label: Use three
steps.title: An explicit withdrawal
steps.text: Remove three fine units. Remaining stock is one pack and seventeen small units.
steps.keep: This withdrawal accounts for the change in total stock.

steps.label: Regroup
steps.title: Only whole packets can cross
steps.text: Request regrouping of seventeen fine units. Ten become one pack; seven remain in their fine basis.
steps.keep: The seven-unit remainder is not rounded away.

steps.label: Draw ten
steps.title: The fine store cannot yet pay in full
steps.text: Drawing ten from seven fine units reaches zero and leaves three units of unpaid demand as negative tension.
steps.keep: The coarse stock exists, but a fine-side draw alone does not silently open a pack.

steps.label: Borrow
steps.title: Choose a route that can pay the draw
steps.text: Explicitly opening one pack supplies ten fine units. Three settle the unpaid demand and seven remain.
steps.keep: The fulfilled withdrawals total thirteen. Together with seventeen remaining units they account for the original thirty.

demos.title: Try a response, keep the alternative
demos.blurb: Blend two inputs, expose a mismatch, and watch one chosen response stall at its resolution.
demos.context: A local space receives light and heat. It can combine these into a signal without needing to name the larger situation. A requested signal gives one experiment a reason to adjust its mixture.
demos.focus: Roots 2–4: partial mixture, alternative, goal, response routes and feedback recipe.
demos.validation: The fixture predicts 8 → 9 → 9 → 10, introducing signed gain changes through carrier settlement. The half-response stall retains one error tick and the alternative mixture survives.
demos.limit: The driver chooses the gain to change and when to try the stronger route. Agreement on this sample is not proof of truth or a general learning rule.

steps.label: Two contributions
steps.title: A local prediction meets a request
steps.text: Half of light 6 contributes 3. A heat gain of 5/10 contributes 5. The mixture predicts 8 against the requested 10.
steps.keep: An alternative mixture already gives 10. Neither result assigns fault or proves the model.

steps.label: Half response
steps.title: One selected participant changes
steps.text: The chosen response turns two mismatch ticks into one gain tick. A new observation at gain 6 predicts 9.
steps.keep: The gain changes through tension. Source observations and the requested result stay connected.

steps.label: Stall
steps.title: The same route cannot make a whole tick
steps.text: One remaining mismatch tick is too small for a whole gain tick through the 2:1 response. The result stays at 9.
steps.result: No gain change · one tick of route residue
steps.keep: Stalling is a visible outcome. There is no hidden minimum step to force progress.

steps.label: Revise route
steps.title: Try an explicitly different experiment
steps.text: The driver chooses the authored 1:1 route. Gain reaches 7 and prediction reaches 10; the earlier attempts and alternative remain.
steps.keep: Agreement on one sample does not make the two mixtures equivalent on future inputs.

demos.title: Cancel units without erasing the standard
demos.blurb: Read miles per hour and litres per hundred kilometres with their authored scales intact.
demos.context: A journey combines speed with elapsed time. A fuel calculation uses litres per 100 km. Both invite cancellation, but a matching dimension is not permission to ignore its tick scale.
demos.focus: Roots 1–4: explicit dimensional cancellation, authored order and the 100 km standard.
demos.validation: The selected cancellation read records one matched hour pair, preserves both authored orders and the standard, refuses km versus 100 km cancellation, and accepts matching 100 km ticks.
demos.limit: This example reads unit participation. It does not divide current values, convert quantities implicitly, or establish the domain for numeric division.

steps.label: Speed × time
steps.title: Select a dimensional read
steps.text: In (mile × hour) / hour, a compatible hour occurrence can cancel. A correspondence records the matched pair and the standard stays attached.
steps.keep: The authored expression remains available; cancellation is an explicit observation.

steps.label: Authored order
steps.title: A commutative read retains its source
steps.text: (hour × mile) / hour can give the same selected unit result. It still has a different authored numerator order.
steps.result: Same unit result · distinct ordered sources
steps.keep: This permission applies to the dimensional read, not arbitrary ordered transformations.

steps.label: Different tick scales
steps.title: One kilometre is not one hundred kilometres
steps.text: A kilometre tick cannot simply cancel the hundred-kilometre denominator tick. Their common dimension does not remove the factor of 100.
steps.keep: Converting a quantity into the chosen standard needs its own calibration and remainder.

steps.label: Matching standard
steps.title: The correspondence now accounts for the scale
steps.text: When both occurrences use hundred-kilometre ticks, the selected pair can cancel. The litre unit and original standard remain.
steps.keep: This is dimensional accounting, with no numeric division or material transfer performed.
